Source: github.com/Humanitariansai/Mycroft PR #16, format-report.js + test-format-report.js. Cycle 1 builds scoreToRating() alone; cycle 2 wires it into an additive camelCaseReport nested object, motivated by the real 'Google Sheet auto-maps by column name' constraint documented in test-format-report.js.

output: scoreToRating() added â€” AAA to D

beats.role_note: the problem, the context, the stakes â€” BEFORE the CLI loop, no composer yet
beats.narration_text: Format Report already outputs a risk score and an alert level â€” INFO up to CRITICAL. Useful, but flat. And this repo's own test file says why you can't just bolt a new field on top: fourteen snake_case keys that a Google Sheet auto-maps by column name. Break that shape, and you silently break someone's automation.
beats.visual_intent: title card: the existing Format Report output (14 snake_case fields, a risk_score, an alert_level) with a Google Sheet icon auto-mapping columns to field names; no composer yet

beats.narration_text: First ask: give the score a rating. Bond-style â€” AAA down to D â€” computed from the same zero-to-hundred-plus number Format Report already has. Nothing new to measure, just a new way to read what's already there.

props.command: claude "add a scoreToRating(riskScore) function to format-report.js: bond-style tiers, AAA best down to D worst, using the same 0-to-100-plus risk score"
props.segment: A Credit Rating for a Risk Score

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat â€” the ACTUAL generated function, shown in full (short enough not to trim)
beats.narration_text: Nine tiers, one number, checked top-down: a hundred or above is D, the worst; below ten is AAA, the best. It mirrors the alert thresholds â€” seventy, forty, twenty â€” but cuts them finer, the way a bond rating cuts finer than pass or fail.

props.title: format-report.js â€” scoreToRating()

beats.role_note: OPEN vox slot â†’ Manim video, real boundary table from test-format-report.js RATING_CASES
beats.narration_text: Sweep the whole range against the real test table. Nine, still AAA. Ten, AA. Twenty, A. Thirty, BBB. Forty, BB. Fifty-five, B. Seventy, CCC. Eighty-five, CC. A hundred, D. Every boundary the tests actually check, snapping into its band.
beats.visual_intent: Manim: a labeled number line 0â€“150 with the nine rating bands colored by severity; a marker sweeps across the exact boundary scores from RATING_CASES (0,9,10,19,20,29,30,39,40,54,55,69,70,84,85,99,100,150), snapping to its band label at each one

beats.narration_text: Now wire it in â€” but nest it. Add a camelCaseReport object: every field mirrored in camelCase, plus the new creditRating. Leave the original fourteen keys exactly as they are. That constraint isn't stylistic â€” it's the Google Sheet's column map talking.

props.command: claude "wire scoreToRating into formatReport(): add a camelCaseReport object nesting every field in camelCase plus creditRating. Additive only â€” don't rename or remove any of the 14 original snake_case keys, the RiskLog Google Sheet auto-maps to them by name"
props.segment: A Credit Rating for a Risk Score

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat â€” REAL formatReport() source, trimmed with literal elision (no rewritten/paraphrased lines)
beats.narration_text: Read the return statement. The top: timestamp, ticker, risk score â€” fourteen keys, untouched, same order, same values. Then, new: camelCaseReport, a full second copy of the same data in camelCase, with one field neither copy had before â€” creditRating, from the function you just watched.

props.title: format-report.js â€” formatReport()

beats.act: OUTPUT â€” cycle 2, the better run
beats.role_note: OPEN vox slot â†’ Manim video, real assertions from test-format-report.js
beats.narration_text: Run the whole test file. Fourteen original keys, present, unchanged, values identical to before â€” all four alert tiers pass. Beside them, camelCaseReport: exactly fifteen keys, every one genuinely camelCase, and creditRating matching the boundary table beat for beat. Nothing removed. Nothing renamed. One thing added, in its own room.
beats.visual_intent: Manim: the 14 original snake_case keys light up ink-colored and hold ('untouched') while a new labeled box, camelCaseReport, assembles beside them with its 15 camelCase keys, creditRating landing last and matching the B04 sweep's band color

beats.narration_text: The hard part was never the nine if-statements. It was making the addition provably additive â€” nest the new shape instead of reshaping the old one, and let a test assert the original key set can never drift, instead of trusting memory that nothing broke.
beats.visual_intent: recap card: 'reshape -> breaks the sheet' vs 'nest -> additive'; the two OUTPUT frames (B04 sweep, B07 merge) side by side
